commits.author: rjpower
commits.message:
[levanter] Avoid retaining checkpoint host copies (#8609)

Stage unsliced GPU checkpoint shards through a transient pinned-host JAX
array before materializing NumPy. This prevents checkpoint
materialization from retaining a host-value cache on the training-owned
source shard. Sliced shards and TPU keep their current paths.

A two-GB200, 100-step synthetic run saved a checkpoint and ran normal
plus dropless evaluation every step. Across both ranks, the
post-evaluation RSS floor slope fell from 11.0 to 3.6 MiB/step. The
median floor increase between the first and last 15 measured steps fell
from 0.93 to 0.27 GiB.
[Control](https://iris.oa.dev/#/job/%2Fpower%2Fcodex-hostmem-micro-main-off-r1-20260823-coord)
and
[treatment](https://iris.oa.dev/#/job/%2Fpower%2Fcodex-hostmem-micro-fixed-off-r1-20260823-coord)
retain the raw logs. The profiling harness and residual-growth
investigation remain in #8599.

---------

Co-authored-by: rjpower <rjpower@users.noreply.github.com>

commits.author: rjpower
commits.message:
[training] Initialize JAX before CuTeDSL cache setup (#8608)

Initialize JAX distributed before importing the CuTeDSL adapter. The
adapter can query `jax.devices()` at import time; the synthetic smoke
job initialized XLA before Iris called `jax.distributed.initialize()`
and failed before training.

Run `FineStoreDirectory`'s interpreter-exit sync on its existing daemon
and wait at most 10 seconds. Explicit close still waits for and
publishes the final file set. The previous `atexit` callback opened S3
synchronously through `fsspec` after Python shut down
`concurrent.futures`, leaving the failed process blocked in FineStore
flush.

Incident: https://echo.oa.dev/wiki/225

---------

Co-authored-by: rjpower <rjpower@users.noreply.github.com>

commits.author: rjpower
commits.message:
[echo] Show useful context for search results (#8607)

Print each Echo search result as a header followed by one primary source
excerpt capped at 240 characters. The excerpt no longer shares a
fixed-width
row with the grading key, qualified source ID, and title. Long
identifiers
therefore cannot reduce useful context to the 20-character minimum.

The reported host-memory query still returns eight results. Its first
issue
excerpt expands from `Full accounting of gr…` to about 200 source
characters, and the checkpoint host-memory wiki result shows its
complete
applicability sentence.

A local replay captured 505 fixed results for all 80 checked-in
benchmark
queries. Across 60 presentation judgments covering 46 unique cases, the
one-excerpt format was preferred 47 times and scored 4.45/5 for
usefulness
and 4.20/5 for scanability. Two richer formats scored 4.70/5 for
usefulness;
their scanability scores were 2.95 and 3.17. The
[Loom session](https://loom.rjp.io/s/326w47ik) contains the
`echo-result-detail-study` artifact with the local setup, variant
definitions,
per-grader results, exact-query output, and limitations.

Co-authored-by: rjpower <rjpower@users.noreply.github.com>

commits.author: rjpower
commits.message:
[agents] Narrow skill activation (#8494)

Keep all 43 repository skill entrypoints while reducing their total
context
from 5,971 to 5,092 lines, a 14.7% reduction.

Classify activation by task semantics. Direct task matches load without
naming
the skill. Optional resource reservations, persistent monitoring,
multi-session
research, durable artifacts, and costly benchmark workflows require
explicit
requests. Scheduled scrubs and the read-only lint reporter run only from
their
named harnesses or explicit requests. Commit, writing style,
stale-document
updates, and Echo incident publication remain automatic companions or
postconditions; every incident produces a tagged Echo record linked from
its
associated pull request or issue.

Remove duplicated repository policy, generic setup narration, and
repeated
workflow explanation. Retain approval boundaries, costly or destructive
operation guards, behavior-changing commands and flags, source-of-truth
rules,
and workflow state transitions. Preserve decision-relevant examples and
environment-specific caveats, including the known-good TensorBoard scope
settings, Finelog metric semantics, fork-refresh pitfalls, logscan
defaults,
and terminal issue schemas.

commits.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
commits.message:
[canary] Use 10M model with one-day outputs (#8600)

Use a fixed 9,933,376-parameter MoE for both TPU and GPU canaries. The
previous heuristic kept 256 experts and produced a 2.04B-parameter model
whose model-plus-optimizer checkpoint was 22.8 GiB.

Write each run to a unique path under the one-day lifecycle temp prefix.
Disable time-policy checkpoints and their resume search path; retain the
forced final checkpoint, which is about 120 MB at the new size. GCS
metric validation resolves the object key through mirror so Actions can
find the regional output, while S3 remains absolute.

Region locality comes from #8605. Fixes #8595.

Co-authored-by: Russell Power <607207+rjpower@users.noreply.github.com>

commits.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
commits.message:
Restore region-local ferry placement (#8605)

Restore Iris's documented default that a child job with no region
preference inherits the physical region of its parent. The August 23
Tier 2 ferry resolved its temporary cache in us-central2, then scheduled
a worker in europe-west4 after #8396 removed the worker-region metadata
and client fallback five days earlier. Iris workers again expose their
authoritative region after user environment merging; child submission
preserves explicit region choices and the ANY_REGION opt-out.

The TPU ferry now uses the primary requested TPU variant as an empirical
availability reservation for its CPU launcher. This selects among
regions where Iris has observed usable TPU capacity and adds no
hard-coded region. The resolved launcher region then propagates to
training and retries.

The Actions history audit found useful defect signal in all six
purpose-built ferries. This change keeps them, adds missing failure
triage to weekly Datakit Tier 3, and replaces the CoreWeave GPU ferry's
6B-token preparation dependency with the 10M-token prebuilt cache.
Dataset scale is not part of the GPU assertion. CoreWeave data remains
in its canonical east02a prefix, where LOTA caches reads for west04
workers. Tier 1–3 remain on GCP because their distributed and
high-memory coverage does not fit the single west04 CPU node.

Marin Cluster Smoke had zero successful scheduled runs: all 38 runs from
July 17 through August 23 were cancelled around its 100-minute timeout.
The workflow and its Grafana lane are deleted. The underlying tests
remain directly runnable through the cluster-test runbook.

The full audit, failure-to-fix links, methodology, alternatives, and
caveats are in the [GitHub Actions real-resource canary
audit](https://loom.oa.dev/s/ujx6ugrk/artifacts/github-actions-real-resource-audit).
The response procedure and root cause are preserved in [Echo incident
223](https://echo.oa.dev/wiki/223). Small status and performance control
files remain in their existing central GCS paths so the off-cluster
runner can discover the dynamically placed run; large step outputs and
caches inherit the run region.

Validated with the required changed-file lint, formatting, and Pyrefly
gate; 58 focused Iris placement/worker tests; the CoreWeave THD canary
construction test; four Grafana nightly-projection tests; and Marin's
affected-test selection. The affected suite passed 4,233 tests with one
unrelated xdist worker crash in test_viz_lm; that test passed when rerun
alone. Live-cluster tests were not run locally.

Co-authored-by: Russell Power <607207+rjpower@users.noreply.github.com>

commits.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
commits.message:
[iris] Propagate supervised rank failures (#8593)

Use one clean-exit handler on every process in an Iris JAX world. The
handler skips finalization when an exception is active, performs
coordinated JAX shutdown with a 120-second bound, and then invokes the
optional global-rank-zero `CompleteJob` callback. If shutdown raises, it
terminates the process with status 1 instead of letting Python preserve
exit 0.

Three 16-rank GB200 restore benchmarks emitted every final `RESULT`
line, then recorded `JobCompletedTaskSucceeded` four to six seconds
before supervisors received SIGTERM and later reaped local ranks at -6
or -9. The same ordering occurred in one-replica, HBM one-replica, and
every-replica restores, isolating teardown accounting from restore
collective behavior.

When every rank reaches JAX shutdown cleanly, rank zero completes the
gang and Iris reports success. A child that exits nonzero, is signaled,
maps a recovery exception, or fails bounded shutdown prevents that
completion call. The multi-GPU supervisor reports a nonzero task exit,
and Iris applies its normal retry policy; an exhausted task fails and
the job cannot succeed.

Incident: https://echo.oa.dev/wiki/217

Original reproduction:
https://iris.oa.dev/#/job/%2Fapp%2Frestore-d1536-one-r2-coord

---------

Co-authored-by: Russell Power <607207+rjpower@users.noreply.github.com>

commits.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
commits.message:
[iris] Retry unknown Kubernetes pod phases as worker loss (#8587)

Hold empty and `Unknown` Kubernetes pod phases for three consecutive
reconciliation polls before ending the attempt as `WORKER_FAILED`. A
transient empty phase in the 704-GPU hero run was previously recorded as
an application `FAILED` attempt, consuming user failure quota and
bouncing all 176 gang members.

Share the grace counter with missing-pod handling and reset it whenever
Kubernetes returns `Pending`, `Running`, `Succeeded`, or `Failed`.
Persistent unknown observations retain the pod identity and a
`PodUnknown` terminal reason while charging the preemption budget.

Incident: https://echo.oa.dev/wiki/213

---------

Co-authored-by: loom <claude-max-1@openathena.ai>

commits.author: rjpower
commits.message:
iris: tighten disruption telemetry tests (#8604)

The terminal-reason assertion added in #8601 was attached to a
resubmission test, so a propagation regression would report as a replay
failure. This gives terminal-reason mirroring its own federation sync
test and returns the resubmission regression to replay and replacement
only.

The same pass removes redundant disruption-field assertions, trims
telemetry docstrings to their persisted contracts, and states how
provider, system, and boot identifiers should be used during
node-history triage.

Follow-up to [review feedback on
#8601](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/8601#discussion_r3838864918).

commits.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
commits.message:
[levanter] Bound Hero loader fetch requests (#8603)

Fetch Hero training data in four-batch storage requests while retaining
the 512-batch completed queue. Rename `prefetch_size` to
`fetch_batch_size` so request size is distinct from queue capacity. The
shared Trainer retains its existing 32-batch request.

The previous 256-batch request asked each of 704 processes for 4,096
sequences and enqueued nothing until the whole request returned. The
cited retry spent about 30 seconds opening 200 training-component
ledgers, then about 100 seconds waiting for that first data request.
Checkpoint restore, first-step compilation, and an earlier CUDA/NVLink
restart account for the rest of the reported startup interval.

On one GB200 tray with four concurrent processes, the slowest 256-batch
request took 29.1 seconds. Four-batch requests made data available in
3.7 seconds and had a worst-process median of 1.16 seconds per steady
request; retrieving 256 batches took 84.4 seconds. One-batch requests
reached data in 1.34 seconds but took 118.6 seconds for the same 256
batches. First-batch hashes were unchanged across treatments. These
timings compare request sizes on one tray; they do not predict the
absolute result of the next 704-process run.

The open cache-catalog PR #8472 can reduce the separate metadata phase.
This measured four-batch choice supersedes the unmeasured one-batch
proposal in #8439. The production timeline, benchmark jobs, and loader
diagrams are in the [Loom
investigation](https://loom.oa.dev/s/zjeg132h/artifacts/hero-dataloader-startup);
the reusable diagnostic is in [Echo](https://echo.oa.dev/wiki/222).

---------

Co-authored-by: Russell Power <607207+rjpower@users.noreply.github.com>

commits.author: rjpower
commits.message:
iris: retain Kubernetes disruption evidence (#8601)

Kubernetes' `DeletionByTaintManager` reason identifies the eviction
mechanism but loses the initiating node fault after the pod and node are
garbage-collected. Record `DisruptionTarget` as `k8s/disruption` in
`iris.task_event`, together with stable pod and node identity, deletion
timing, tolerations, taints, health conditions, and selected hardware
and provider metadata. Retry failed Finelog writes and emit an enriched
row when a temporarily unavailable node snapshot appears. Retain task
events for up to 30 days under the existing 1 GiB cap.

Federation now preserves the member controller's pod name, pod UID, node
name, and terminal reason when mirroring attempt history, so the hub
task view retains its backend evidence.

The fleet investigation found 17 attempts with this exact terminal text
across 15 nodes. Three attempts on one node were evicted together during
a single drain; no node had the exact eviction at multiple distinct
times. The triggering incident and response guidance are recorded in
[Echo](https://echo.oa.dev/wiki/221).

commits.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
commits.message:
[levanter] Restore replicated checkpoint shards once (#8589)

On GPU and CPU, read each unique checkpoint shard on one replica and
distribute
it across the replica axes with a JAX reduction. On the 704-rank Grug
hero,
each rank read 91.19 GiB during the cold step-7459 restore: 62.69 TiB of
addressable reads for a 4.88 TiB checkpoint, or 12.85x amplification.

Hash reader selection by array path and shard index so S3 reads remain
spread
across the 11 replica groups. Replicas stage zeros alongside the
selected
TensorStore shard in accelerator memory, reduce the leading replica
dimension,
and return the result to its original device or pinned-host memory kind.
Deterministic, memory-bounded batches keep every rank in the same
collective
order. The collective reduces unsigned bytes so signed zero, NaN
payloads, and
subnormal values remain bit-exact. `every_replica` remains available in
the
restore benchmark as a control.

An eight-device test with two replicas lowers TensorStore chunk reads
from 16
to 8 and preserves pinned-host output. A two-process JAX test reads two
replicated chunks once each across the fleet. TPU keeps the established
every-replica path because JAX 0.11 aborts when a collective returns
pinned-host buffers.

A four-node GB200 d1536 benchmark used an eight-device expert mesh with
two
replica groups. The [replica-aware
run](https://iris.oa.dev/#/job/%2Fapp%2Frestore-d1536-one-hbm-r2-coord)
read 108.92 GiB from TensorStore across 16 ranks; the

[control](https://iris.oa.dev/#/job/%2Fapp%2Frestore-d1536-every-r2-coord)
read 257.28 GiB, a 57.7% reduction. Peak staging was 14.75 GiB against
the
16 GiB process budget, and XLA emitted no host-compute lowering
warnings.
Cold and warm restore times were 6.9 and 3.6 seconds, against 4.7 and
4.3
seconds for the control. This small run did not saturate object storage,
so it
validates traffic reduction and memory placement. Hero-scale latency
remains
unmeasured. Both jobs emitted every result before JAX distributed
teardown
aborted ranks; Iris incorrectly recorded those exits as successful,
tracked
separately in Loom issue 283.

Echo [incident 205](https://echo.oa.dev/wiki/205) records the earlier
306 Gb/s
cold restore burst.

---------

Co-authored-by: Russell Power <607207+rjpower@users.noreply.github.com>
